# laravel_cloud_database_user (Resource)

Manages a user in a Laravel Cloud database cluster, with read and write or read-only access to some of its databases. Laravel MySQL and AWS RDS clusters support database users; Serverless Postgres does not.

~> **Beta:** This provider is in beta. Its resources and attributes may change between releases, so pin the provider version and read the changelog before you upgrade.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "laravel_cloud_database_user" "reporting" {
  cluster_id = laravel_cloud_database_cluster.example.id
  username   = "reporting"
  type       = "read_only"
  databases  = [laravel_cloud_database.example.id]
}

# The password is generated by Laravel Cloud and returned only when the user
# is created; Terraform keeps it in state.
output "reporting_password" {
  value     = laravel_cloud_database_user.reporting.password
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) Database cluster ID.
- `databases` (Set of String) IDs of the databases in the cluster the user may access, such as `laravel_cloud_database.example.id`. An empty set grants access to none. Changed in place. Deleting one of these databases removes it from the user's access.
- `type` (String) `read_write` or `read_only`. Changed in place.
- `username` (String) Username. Starts with a lowercase letter or underscore and contains only lowercase letters, digits and underscores; 3 to 32 characters on MySQL clusters, 3 to 63 on Postgres. It must be unused in the cluster, and engine-reserved names are refused. Changing it replaces the user.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String)
- `id` (String) Database user ID.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Generated password. The API returns it only when the user is created, so it is kept in state from then on; an imported user has none.
- `status` (String) Status: `creating`, `available`, `failed` or `deleted`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Database users are addressed through their cluster, so the import ID is
# composite. An imported user has no password in state: the API returns it
# only when the user is created. The cluster's superuser cannot be imported.
terraform import laravel_cloud_database_user.example "{cluster_id}:{user_id}"
```
